vision: drawgen becomes the engineer's one run from a finished SOLIDWORKS assembly to everything the shop and the estimator need: native, checked drawings for every part, the parts list with lengths, areas and mass, and a list of exactly which sheets a model change touches, all measured from the solid and traced to the datum or rule that placed it. The designer decides views, datums and tolerances; drawgen does the rest and flags what it will not guess.

patterns.title: Show the result on the buyer's own model in the first meeting
patterns.text: The drawing and CPQ tools that sell into engineering let the buyer see output on their own files before any commitment: DraftAid runs 15-minute demos on models the prospect brings, and DriveWorks Solo offers a 30-day full trial with no credit card. Engineers in drawgen's calls say the same thing in reverse: they reserve judgement on price until they see it work.

evidence.text: DraftAid offers personalised 15-minute demos where prospects bring their own models and see drawings generated in seconds; no pricing is published.
DriveWorks Solo is sold with a free 30-day full-feature trial, instant access and no credit card, above the free DriveWorksXpress inside SOLIDWORKS.
Customers value automated, accurate dimensioning that meets ISO standards on complex parts, but reserve judgement on price and adoption until they see it work.

patterns.title: Automate the first pass, keep the engineer as the decision-maker
patterns.text: The AI features gaining ground in manufacturing software stop short of deciding. Paperless Parts' Wingman surfaces GD&T and critical callouts for an estimator to resolve, CoLab's AutoReview runs a first-pass check against the company's own standards, and Tacton's modelling assistant hands over a model 70 to 80 percent complete for human review. This is the same shape as drawgen's abstention: fill what can be measured, flag what needs judgement.

evidence.text: Paperless Parts Requirements Review extracts GD&T and critical callouts from prints, flags high-risk conditions with custom rules and routes them to estimators, who stay the decision-makers.
CoLab AutoReview runs first-pass checks on drawings and 3D models, trained on the organisation's standards and past review lessons, inside SOLIDWORKS, Creo, NX and PLM integrations.
Tacton's AI Product Modeling Assistant turns spreadsheets and PDFs into CPQ models typically 70 to 80 percent complete before human review.

patterns.title: Name the job and the department, then prove it in their numbers
patterns.text: Tacto sells one thing to one buyer, the AI for industrial procurement, and leads with spend managed and savings; CADDi leads with hours saved and procurement cost cut. Neither sells an abstract platform first, and VSI notes CADDi's valuation re-rated only after workflow products sat on its data layer.

evidence.text: Tacto positions as the AI for industrial procurement, sold to procurement teams and CPOs, and leads with EUR 1 billion of spend managed and 75 percent time saved.
CADDi leads with customer outcomes such as 100,000 hours saved at an automotive OEM and 30 percent annual procurement cost reduction at a machinery maker.
CADDi's valuation was flat for three and a half years as a searchable drawing archive and re-rated only after the platform and agent layer existed.

patterns.text: Leo AI, which integrates with SOLIDWORKS and SOLIDWORKS PDM, leads with SOC 2, GDPR and zero training on customer data, and REV1 is flagged in VSI for pairing GD&T with SOC 2. drawgen already runs in-process with geometry staying on the machine, and a design manager asked about the vault before anything else.

problem.title: Assemblies, views and datums are where drawing tools fail
problem.text: The strongest signal in VSI, decision-grade across seven conversations and three firms, is that existing tools do not handle large assemblies and that any automation must infer the process to set zero points and datums. SOLIDWORKS auto-dimensioning was tried and dropped for exactly that reason, and senior engineers name wrong datums and views as the first thing they send back.

evidence.text: Customers want to automate drawing creation, but existing tools do not handle large assemblies, and a solution must infer manufacturing processes to set correct zero points and datums. Decision-grade, 7 conversations, 3 companies.

trends.title: CAD vendors now ship drawing automation in the box
trends.text: SOLIDWORKS 2026 adds generative Drawing Creation that builds views, dimensions, hole callouts and the sheet format, reported generally available from July 2026, and Autodesk Fusion has automated drawings since January 2024, which Autodesk puts at about 60 percent of the drawing work. Neither is reported to handle datums or tolerances, which is where drawgen's calls say the time goes, but the default expectation that SOLIDWORKS will ship this natively is now a fact to design around.

evidence.text: SOLIDWORKS 2026 announces generative AI that speeds up drawing creation and detailing, plus fastener recognition in assemblies.
Generative Drawing Creation builds views, dimensions, hole callouts and sheet format from a part or assembly, general availability July 2026; the article does not address GD&T or datums.
Autodesk Fusion automated drawings create part and assembly drawings in minutes but need manual refinement; Autodesk estimates about 60 percent of the drawing work.
Engineers' default expectation is that SOLIDWORKS will eventually ship automated drawings natively. Risk register: high severity, high likelihood.

trends.title: The EU Machinery Regulation makes the technical file digital from 20 January 2027
trends.text: Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 replaces the Machinery Directive on 20 January 2027, allows digital instructions by default and keeps documentation accessible for at least ten years. A UK machine builder's contact believes machines built now for delivery after January already need it, which turns traceable, model-derived documentation into a dated buying trigger.

evidence.text: Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 20 January 2027 and expands documentation duties: technical files, risk assessments, instructions and declarations kept accurate, traceable and retained.
Digital instructions become the permitted default, with paper on request and online access for at least ten years.

trends.title: AI quoting and CPQ move to human-reviewed, rule-backed output
trends.text: In 2025 and 2026 the quoting and CPQ leaders shipped AI that prepares and the human approves: Tacton's modelling assistant (May 2026) and Paperless Parts' Requirements Review (general availability October 2025). trends.text: Manufacturers adopting model-based definition mostly run a hybrid, keeping drawings next to annotated models and sharing PMI through STEP AP242. initiatives.title: Fabrication first: plate, profile and weldment rules
initiatives.summary: Ship drawing rules per process family, starting with the simplest high-volume ones (laser-cut plates, standard steel profiles, weldments), so each sheet carries the dimensions its process needs, such as edge-to-hole, cut length and bevel.

initiatives.summary: A procurement-facing agent that routes drawgen's parts list to preferred suppliers and collects quotes, sold to purchasing departments through co-hosted regional meetups.
initiatives.bet: We believe that procurement holds a bigger budget than the drawing office and would buy a sourcing agent fed by the model. We will know when a purchasing head at a German machine builder commits to a pilot.
initiatives.problem: Supplier choice follows designer habit, and wrong deliveries cost weeks; VSI's next step proposes selling to procurement in Germany.
risks: Parked: the procurement case rests on E2 desk research, while no purchasing buyer has been interviewed; the drawing office has the E4 and E5 evidence.
Parked: Tacto already sells exactly this to industrial procurement with EUR 1 billion of spend managed.
Parked: a design engineer called supplier routing too wide, since each firm links suppliers in PDM or ERP already.
initiatives.firstMove: None for now. Keep the parts list exportable so a procurement tool can consume it, and interview two purchasing heads before reconsidering.

evidence.text: Next step: target German procurement departments via co-hosted meetups; procurement holds a bigger budget than the drawing office (desk research).
Tacto: the AI for industrial procurement, EUR 1 billion of spend managed, 75 percent time saved.
the amount of stuff we've had arrive and it's wrong and we have to send it back and wait another 4 weeks.

initiatives.title: One run per assembly, views and datums set once
initiatives.summary: drawgen reads the whole assembly, proposes a sheet and views for every unique part, and asks the designer to confirm views and click datums and a tolerance class once before it dimensions everything.
initiatives.bet: We believe that letting the designer confirm views and datums for a whole assembly in one pass, then dimensioning every part from those choices, will get design offices at ETO machine builders to release drawgen sheets without redrawing. We will know when a design partner releases a full assembly's part drawings with fewer returns than their own baseline.
initiatives.problem: Existing tools handle single parts, not assemblies, and fail on views and datums, which is exactly what checkers send back; SOLIDWORKS auto-dimensioning was dropped for being unreadable.
risks: SOLIDWORKS generative Drawing Creation handles assemblies well enough that a separate add-in is not worth paying for.
Designers skip the confirmation step, which would mean the datum choice is not the value but a chore.
Datum choices vary so much by fixturing that one click per part is not enough to dimension correctly.
initiatives.firstMove: Take one design partner's real assembly, run it with a view-and-datum confirmation screen built as a clickable mock over real drawgen output, and have their checker mark each sheet as release, fix or redraw. Compare against the same assembly run through SOLIDWORKS 2026 Drawing Creation.

evidence.text: Existing tools do not handle large assemblies, and any new solution must infer manufacturing processes to set correct zero points and datums. Decision-grade, 7 conversations, 3 companies.
Well, what happens if I've got a whole assembly that I need to draw?
If you get that wrong, the whole drawing is crap, right?
The biggest issue I have when somebody else creates a drawing is they pick the wrong dimension, the wrong datums.
SOLIDWORKS DimXpert needs the user to specify datums before it can dimension.
SOLIDWORKS 2026 generative Drawing Creation builds views, dimensions and hole callouts from a part or assembly; GD&T and datums are not addressed.
Decision: the designer picks views, datums and tolerance class; drawgen does the rest.

initiatives.title: Costed parts list from the same assembly
initiatives.summary: One click turns the assembly into a classified, measured parts list (profiles with cut lengths, plates with area and thickness, machined parts, bought-in items, coating areas and mass), renamed where names are unusable, which the estimator prices with their own rates and exports to Excel.
initiatives.bet: We believe that a parts list measured from the solid, with the estimator's own rates applied line by line, will replace the hand extraction into Excel for sales engineers at ETO machine builders and fabricators. We will know when two design partners send a real quote built from it and say which lines they had to correct.
initiatives.problem: Engineers extract part data from the 3D model into Excel by hand for every quote because badly named components make the BOM unusable, taking 2 to 4 hours per assembly.
risks: Estimators need rates and routings that do not exist in the model, so the list saves the easy part and leaves the hard one.
Small builders do not pay for it: a manufacturing investor says quoting tools for sub-100-person firms fail on missing data.
PDM or ERP BOM exports are good enough once parts are named properly, which is a process fix, not a product.
initiatives.firstMove: Rebuild the heavy-fabrication checker's 33-part platform extraction with drawgen's geometry read (lengths, coating areas, mass, grouping by profile) and time it against their 2 to 3 hours. Show the Excel export to the UK handling-equipment builder and ask which columns their estimator fills next.

evidence.text: Engineers manually extract part data from 3D models into Excel for quoting, 2 to 4 hours per assembly, because BOMs are unusable due to improper naming. Decision-grade, 4 conversations, 3 of 4 learnings E4.
there were like 33 parts to extract from a model. I had to verify everything, so it took roughly 2 to 3 hours for me to wrap it up and put it on Excel sheet
Because almost 70% of the data that you need to create the asset does not exist.
Whereas you can't really do that with bespoke products. We've tried, we've tried.
Paperless Parts prices from a configurable geometric pricing engine with part file analysis, for job shops and contract manufacturers.
DriveWorks generates order-specific parts, drawings, BOMs and quotes, but for rule-defined configurable product families.
Decision: make the costed parts list the second product, not an AI price.
